data.question_title: The roots of the equation \(\sqrt{3x+1} +1=\sqrt{x} \) are
data.explanation_txt:
Given equation is \(\sqrt{3x+1} +1=\sqrt{x} \)

\[\Rightarrow \sqrt{3x+1} =\sqrt{x} -1\]

Squaring on both sides, we get \(3x+1=x+1-2\sqrt{x} \)

\(\Rightarrow 2\sqrt{x} +2x=0 \\ \Rightarrow \sqrt {x}(1 + \sqrt{x}) = 0 \\ \Rightarrow x = 0 \) \( [ \) Since, \( \sqrt{x} \ge 0 \forall \, x \in \mathbb{R} \), \( (1+\sqrt{x}) \ne 0 \) \( ] \)

But, \(x = 0 \) doesn't satisfy original equation. So, no root.

  • very dilute acid: \( Zn + 10HNO_3 \to Zn(NO_3)_2 + NH_4NO_3 + 3H_2O \)
  • dilute acid: \( 4Zn + 10HNO_3 \to 4Zn(NO_3)_2+N_2O+5H_2O\)
  • moderately concentrated acid: \(3Zn + 8HNO_3 \to 3Zn(NO_3)_2+2NO+4H_2O \)
  • concentrated acid: \(Zn + 4HNO_3 \to Zn(NO_3)_2 + 2NO_2 + 2H_2O \)
